text:
maya: Hey SRE — us-west-2a GPU pool showing ~20% pod restarts and pod startup >30s over the last 15m. Egress latency spikes to ~400ms. Thinking partial zonal evac. Thoughts? :warning:
chen: saw the alerts, and I also see AZ-to-AZ network errors for pods pinned to pool-a. Could be NIC saturation or PCI resets.
alex: can we confirm node events? spot reclaim? kernel OOM?
ops-bot: alert: gpu-pool-usw2a-high-restarts (P2) — 20 alerts in 15m. https://dash.redwood/internal/d/gpu-pools/usw2a
maya: grabbing node logs, attaching a quick snippet:
```
Feb 28 14:12:02 kubelet kubelet: eviction: node not ready for pods
[dmesg] mlx5_core: CQ overrun, hw error, reset scheduled
Feb 28 14:13:10 kubelet: docker: container start fail: network plugin error
```
kai: if it's hardware/NIC, draining the whole AZ might be faster than slow patching, but cross-AZ egress and Dedicated customer placement makes that costly.
chen: agree. proposal: cordon pool-a, drain non-prod & spot first, then move a small prod canary (10%) and observe. escalate to wider drain only if canary still shows tail latency.
lena: how will we shift LB weights? rwd-router supports weighted routing. we should also cold-cache embeddings to avoid recompute storm while we shift.
alex: commands I'm going to run (dry-run first):
```bash
# cordon pool-a
redwoodctl node pool set-scheduling --pool=usw2a-gpu --sched=false
# drain spot nodes first
redwoodctl node drain --pool=usw2a-gpu --priority=spot --timeout=600s
```
maya: starting spot drain now. notifying Dedicated leads. :phone:
partners-bot: DM -> #dedicated-customers: "We're proactively shifting some capacity due to a partial AZ networking degradation in us-west-2a. No API key changes expected. We'll update if anything changes."
alex: finance reminder: cross-AZ egress will increase costs — rough estimate +12% for affected traffic if we keep traffic in other AZs for ~3h. worth flagging.
chen: also disable autoscaler bursts toward pool-a to avoid provisioning into a degraded AZ:
```bash
redwoodctl autoscaler set --pool=usw2a-gpu --scale-burst=0
```
kai: after spot drain completes, start controlled drain of low-priority prod shards:
```bash
redwoodctl drain --pool=usw2a-gpu --labels="priority=low-prod" --parallel=2
```
maya: spot drain finished — immediate drop in restarts from 20 -> 6. latency still high on remaining prod pods (tail).
lena: ok shift 25% of prod traffic off pool-a via rwd-router weight change and monitor for 5m. if errors down, continue.
maya: weight change applied. monitoring now — error rate 5m window -> 2.8% to 1.1%, tail latency down ~200ms. promising.
alex: good. next steps: open ticket with cloud provider for NIC replacement/replacement schedule, plan AZ maintenance window, and prepare rollback (re-enable scheduling) if shifting makes things worse. flag Dedicated customers for potential SLA impact if we end up with a full evac.
chen: filing ticket now, attaching node list + syslogs, tag=cloud-support-urgent.
maya: leaving pool cordoned for now. will update when provider responds. :thumbsup:
incident-tracker: created INC-2027-0043 "usw2a GPU pool partial evac" assigned to chen.
alex: +1. nice run. once provider confirms hardware level fault we'll decide full zone drain vs targeted remediation. keep this thread for comms.
